question.questionText: By the time I'm seventy, I hope I __________________.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank in the sentence 'By the time I'm seventy, I hope I __________.' requires the use of the future perfect tense. The phrase 'By the time' is often used with the future perfect to indicate that an action will be completed before a specific time in the future. The structure for the future perfect is 'will have + past participle.'
  • will have retired (verb phrase (future perfect)): This is the future perfect tense (will have + past participle). It means the action of retiring will be completed before the speaker turns seventy.
  • will have been retiring (verb phrase (future perfect continuous)): This is the future perfect continuous tense (will have been + V-ing). It is used to show that an action will have been happening for a period of time up to a point in the future, but 'retire' is not usually used in the continuous form because it is a one-time event.
  • will be retiring (verb phrase (future continuous)): This is the future continuous tense (will be + V-ing). It means the action will be in progress at a specific time in the future, but with 'by the time,' we need to show completion, not an ongoing action.
Related structure or vocabulary: By the time + future perfect (will have + past participle): used to show that something will be finished before a certain time in the future.

  • will have retired (cụm động từ (thì tương lai hoàn thành)): Đây là thì tương lai hoàn thành (will have + quá khứ phân từ). Nghĩa là hành động nghỉ hưu sẽ hoàn thành trước khi người nói 70 tuổi.
  • will have been retiring (cụm động từ (thì tương lai hoàn thành tiếp diễn)): Đây là thì tương lai hoàn thành tiếp diễn (will have been + V-ing). Thì này dùng để diễn tả một hành động sẽ diễn ra liên tục đến một thời điểm trong tương lai, nhưng 'retire' (nghỉ hưu) là hành động xảy ra một lần nên không dùng ở dạng tiếp diễn.
